hello.note: Formal, safe default; used any time of day.

slang.note: Very casual hi/bye for friends and peers; signals ty-terms, skip with strangers in formal settings.
Casual bye (borrowed from ciao); fine for friends and equals, too familiar for a boss or clerk.

how_are_you.note: Polite 'vy' form for someone you do not know.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'not for what'; standard reply to thanks.

no_problem.note: Casual everyday phrase, popular with younger speakers.

slang.note: Even more relaxed reply meaning 'it's all good/no worries'; warm and safe with anyone in a casual moment.

of_course.note: Standard emphatic 'of course' to a request; not a literal calque.

slang.note: Everyday casual 'sure/of course' among friends and peers; upbeat and fine with most people in a relaxed moment.
Upbeat everyday slang for 'awesome/great'; fine with anyone in a casual moment.

delicious.note: Literally 'excellent'; the standard way to praise tasty food or drink.

slang.note: Playful 'yum!' interjection said before or while eating; warm and kid-friendly, fine with anyone.

cheers.note: Hold eye contact while clinking glasses; skipping it is considered bad luck.
